The **2024 Pulitzer Prizes** were awarded by the [Pulitzer Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulitzer_Prize "Pulitzer Prize") Board for work during the 2023 calendar year on May 6, 2024.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Pulitzer_Prize#cite_note-1)
## Prizes
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2024_Pulitzer_Prize&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Prizes")]
Winners and finalists for the prizes are listed below, with the winners marked in **bold**.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Pulitzer_Prize#cite_note-Pulitzer2024-2)
### Journalism
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2024_Pulitzer_Prize&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Journalism")]  
| [Public Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulitzer_Prize_for_Public_Service "Pulitzer Prize for Public Service") |  
| --- |  
|  _**[ProPublica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ProPublica "ProPublica")**_ , for the work of Joshua Kaplan, Justin Elliott, [Brett Murphy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brett_Murphy "Brett Murphy"), Alex Mierjeski and Kirsten Berg, for "groundbreaking and ambitious reporting that pierced the thick wall of secrecy surrounding the [Supreme Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_United_States "Supreme Court of United States") to reveal how a small group of politically influential billionaires wooed justices with lavish gifts and travel, pushing the Court to adopt its first code of conduct."  |  
|  _[KFF Health News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KFF_Health_News "KFF Health News") and [Cox Media Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cox_Media_Group "Cox Media Group")_, "for uncovering millions of cases in which the Social Security Administration overpaid beneficiaries, then demanded immediate repayment — imposing debts on elderly and disabled people who had already spent the funds."  |  
|  _[The Washington Post](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Washington_Post "The Washington Post")_ , "for its sobering examination of the AR-15 semi-automatic rifle, which forced readers to reckon with the horrors wrought by the weapon often used for mass shootings in America."  |  
| [Breaking News Reporting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulitzer_Prize_for_Breaking_News_Reporting "Pulitzer Prize for Breaking News Reporting") |  
| --- |  
|  **Staff of _[Lookout Santa Cruz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lookout_Santa_Cruz "Lookout Santa Cruz")_ , California**, "for its detailed and nimble community-focused coverage, over a holiday weekend, of catastrophic flooding and mudslides that displaced thousands of residents and destroyed more than 1,000 homes and businesses."  |  
| Staff of the _[Honolulu Civil Beat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honolulu_Civil_Beat "Honolulu Civil Beat")_ , "for its distinctive, sweeping and urgent coverage of [the Maui wildfires](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Hawaii_wildfires "2023 Hawaii wildfires") that killed more than 100 people and left a historic town in ruins, reporting that held officials to account and chronicled the aftermath and efforts to rebuild."  |  
| Staff of the _[Los Angeles Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Times "Los Angeles Times")_ , "for urgent and thoughtful coverage of a Lunar New Year [overnight shooting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Monterey_Park_shooting "2023 Monterey Park shooting") that left 11 senior citizens dead, demonstrating clear knowledge of and commitment to the local Asian communities."  |  
 |  
| [Investigative Reporting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulitzer_Prize_for_Investigative_Reporting "Pulitzer Prize for Investigative Reporting") |  
| --- |  
|  **[Hannah Dreier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hannah_Dreier "Hannah Dreier") of _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times "The New York Times")_** , "for a deeply reported series of stories revealing the stunning reach of migrant child labor across the United States—and the corporate and governmental failures that perpetuate it."  |  
| Casey Ross and Bob Herman of _[STAT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stat_\(website\) "Stat \(website\)")_ , "for exposing how [UnitedHealth Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UnitedHealth_Group "UnitedHealth Group"), the nation's largest health insurer, used an unregulated algorithm to override clinicians' judgments and deny care, highlighting the dangers of AI use in medicine."  |  
| Staff of _[Bloomberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bloomberg_News "Bloomberg News")_ , "for a deep and rigorous investigation of how the US government aided the global spread of gun violence, prompting the [Biden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden "Joe Biden") administration to halt most gun exports for 90 days while it reviewed the federal government's marketing relationship with gun manufacturers."  |  
 |  
| [Explanatory Reporting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulitzer_Prize_for_Explanatory_Reporting "Pulitzer Prize for Explanatory Reporting") |  
| --- |  
|  **[Sarah Stillman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Stillman "Sarah Stillman") of _[The New Yorker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_Yorker "The New Yorker")_** , "for a searing indictment of our legal system’s reliance on the felony murder charge and its disparate consequences, often devastating for communities of color."  |  
| Staff of _Bloomberg_ , "for rigorous, far-reaching reporting that holds corporate water profiteers to account and exposes how they willfully exacerbate the effects of climate change at the expense of less powerful communities."  |  
| Staffs of _[The Texas Tribune](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Texas_Tribune "The Texas Tribune")_ , _ProPublica_ , and _[FRONTLINE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frontline_\(American_TV_program\) "Frontline \(American TV program\)")_ , "for advancing understanding of law enforcement’s catastrophic response to [the mass shooting at a Uvalde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uvalde_school_shooting "Uvalde school shooting"), Texas elementary school and also for documenting the political and policy shortcomings that have led to similar deadly police failures across the country."  |  
 |  
| [Local Reporting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulitzer_Prize_for_Local_Reporting "Pulitzer Prize for Local Reporting") |  
| --- |  
|  **[Sarah Conway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Conway "Sarah Conway") of _[City Bureau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_Bureau "City Bureau")_ and Trina Reynolds-Tyler of the _[Invisible Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invisible_Institute "Invisible Institute")_** , "for their investigative series on missing Black girls and women in Chicago that revealed how systemic racism and police department neglect contributed to the crisis."  |  
| Jerry Mitchell, Ilyssa Daly, Brian Howey and Nate Rosenfield of _[Mississippi Today](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mississippi_Today "Mississippi Today")_ and _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times "The New York Times")_ , "for their detailed examination of corruption and abuse, including the torturing of suspects, by Mississippi sheriffs and their officers over two decades."  |  
| Staff of _[The Villages Daily Sun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Villages_Daily_Sun "The Villages Daily Sun")_ , "for its comprehensive investigation and moment-by-moment account of Florida officials’ inaction before, during and after [Hurricane Ian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Ian "Hurricane Ian"), the deadliest storm to strike the state since 1935."  |  
 |  
| [National Reporting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulitzer_Prize_for_National_Reporting "Pulitzer Prize for National Reporting") |  
| --- |  
|  **Staff of _[Reuters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reuters "Reuters")_** , "for an eye-opening series of accountability stories focused on [Elon Musk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elon_Musk "Elon Musk")’s automobile and aerospace businesses, stories that displayed remarkable breadth and depth and provoked official probes of his companies’ practices in Europe and the United States." **Staff of _[The Washington Post](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Washington_Post "The Washington Post")_** , "for its sobering examination of the AR-15 semi-automatic rifle, which forced readers to reckon with the horrors wrought by the weapon often used for mass shootings in America."  |  
| Bianca Vázquez Toness and Sharon Lurye of the _[Associated Press](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Associated_Press "Associated Press")_ , "for a deeply reported series on the corrosive effect of the pandemic on public education, highlighting the staggering number of students missing from classrooms across America."  |  
| Dave Philipps of _The New York Times_ , "for groundbreaking reporting that uncovered a pattern of traumatic brain injuries among U.S. troops from blast exposures caused by the weapons they were firing."  |  
| [International Reporting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulitzer_Prize_for_International_Reporting "Pulitzer Prize for International Reporting") |  
| --- |  
|  **Staff of _The New York Times_** , "for its wide-ranging and revelatory coverage of [Hamas’ lethal attack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Hamas-led_attack_on_Israel "2023 Hamas-led attack on Israel") in southern Israel on October 7, Israel's intelligence failures and the Israeli military's sweeping, deadly response in Gaza."  |  
| Julie Turkewitz and Federico Rios of _The New York Times_ , "for their immersive and ambitious coverage of "migration purgatory" in the Darién Gap between Colombia and Panama."  |  
| Staff of _The Washington Post_ , "for a sweeping on-the-ground investigation in India that exposed the methodical undermining of the world’s largest democracy by [Narendra Modi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narendra_Modi "Narendra Modi") and his Hindu nationalist allies, who have deployed social media to foment hate and pressure American tech giants to bend to government power."  |  
| [Feature Writing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulitzer_Prize_for_Feature_Writing "Pulitzer Prize for Feature Writing") |  
| --- |  
|  **[Katie Engelhart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katie_Engelhart "Katie Engelhart"), contributing writer, _The New York Times_** , "for her fair-minded portrait of a family’s legal and emotional struggles during a matriarch’s progressive dementia that sensitively probes the mystery of a person’s essential self."  |  
| Jennifer Senior of _[The Atlantic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Atlantic "The Atlantic")_ , "for her exquisitely rendered account of her disabled aunt, who was institutionalized as a small child, and the lasting effects on her family, told in the context of present-day care and intervention that make different outcomes possible."  |  
|  [Keri Blakinger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keri_Blakinger "Keri Blakinger") of _[The Marshall Project](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Marshall_Project "The Marshall Project")_ , "for her insightful, humane portrait, reported with great difficulty, of men on Death Row in Texas who play clandestine games of “Dungeons & Dragons,” countering their extreme isolation with elaborate fantasy. (Co-published with _The New York Times Magazine_.)"  |  
 |  
| [Commentary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulitzer_Prize_for_Commentary "Pulitzer Prize for Commentary") |  
| --- |  
|  **[Vladimir Kara-Murza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vladimir_Kara-Murza "Vladimir Kara-Murza"), contributor, _The Washington Post_** , "for passionate columns written under great personal risk from his prison cell, warning of the consequences of dissent in [Vladimir Putin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vladimir_Putin "Vladimir Putin")'s Russia and insisting on a democratic future for his country."  |  
| Brian Lyman of the _[Alabama Reflector](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alabama_Reflector "Alabama Reflector")_ , "for brave, clear and pointed columns that challenge ever-more-repressive state policies flouting democratic norms and targeting vulnerable populations, written with the command and authority of a veteran political observer."  |  
|  [Jay Caspian Kang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Caspian_Kang "Jay Caspian Kang") of _[The New Yorker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_Yorker "The New Yorker")_ , "for original columns that force us to reexamine popular narratives and reframe such critical topics as affirmative action, racial politics and the portrayal of gun violence."  |  
 |  
| [Criticism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulitzer_Prize_for_Criticism "Pulitzer Prize for Criticism") |  
| --- |  
|  **[Justin Chang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Chang "Justin Chang") of the _[Los Angeles Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Times "Los Angeles Times")_** , "for richly evocative and genre-spanning film criticism that reflects on the contemporary moviegoing experience."  |  
|  [Vinson Cunningham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vinson_Cunningham "Vinson Cunningham") of _The New Yorker_ , "for theater reviews that reflect a formidable knowledge of the stage and the mechanics of performance along with canny observations on the human condition."  |  
|  [Zadie Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zadie_Smith "Zadie Smith"), contributor, _[The New York Review of Books](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Review_of_Books "The New York Review of Books")_ , "for a review of the film “[Tár](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T%C3%A1r "Tár")” that addressed with wit and ease such consequential themes as mortality and the clash of generations."  |  
 |  
| [Editorial Writing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulitzer_Prize_for_Editorial_Writing "Pulitzer Prize for Editorial Writing") |  
| --- |
